 Judgment

This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act claiming for compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:

On 20.01.2022 at about 8.30 a.m. when the petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA 50H9710, near Kugonahalli Gate, Doddabalapura Dabaspete 207 Road, Doddabelavanagala hobli, Doddaballupura taluk, Bengaluru Rural district, at that time, the driver of the Ape Auto bearing Reg. No. KA43 9355 who came from doddaballapura towards Dobbaspete drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly turned towards right side without giving any signal or indication and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle, caused the accident, as a result,
the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Soon after the accident,
petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for the accidental injuries.
3. Further it is contended that, at the time of accident petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 24 years, doing agriculture and business and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/a.m.
Due to accidental injuries, petitioner is suffering from permanent disability.
The accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence prays to award the compensation of rs.40 lakhs from the respondents.
4. In response of Tribunal process, the respondents No.1 and 2 appeared before the Tribunal and the 2nd respondent filed written statement.

Though the 1st respondent appeared through his counsel,
but has not filed written statement.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.
This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of the offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.

Further this respondent has Kantharaju.H vs Ramesh H.P on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189372859/
2 denied the age, occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The alleged accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the rider of the motor cycle and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, on other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.

6. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the bike bearing reg.No.KA439355 on 2012022 at about 8.30 a.m. near Kugonahalli gate, DoddaballapuraDobbaspete 207 road, Doddabelabanagala hobli,
Doddabalapura Taluk, Bengaluru rural district ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got examined three witnesses as PW.2 to PW.4 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P36 documents.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and got marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R7 documents.
8.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My answers to the above issues are as follows: Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following: REASONS 10. Issue No.1: In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA439355, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 9 documents as ExP1 to 9 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, charge sheet,
wound certificate, copy of charge sheet and discharge summary.

11. The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of the complaint lodged by Puttashyamaiah,
S/o.

Late Channappa, the Doddabelavangala police station has conducted thorough investigation and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC at Ex.P6 holding that on 20.01.2022 at about 8.30 a.m. near Kugonahalli Gate, DoddabalapuraDabaspete 207 Road, Doddabelavanagala hobli, Doddaballupura taluk, Bengaluru Rural district,

the driver of the Ape Auto bearing Reg.No.KA439355 who came from Doddaballapura towards Dobbaspete drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly turned towards right side without giving any signal or indication and dashed to the Kantharaju.

H vs Ramesh H.P on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189372859/
3
petitioner's vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA50 H9710, caused the accident, as a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

12. On perusal of Ex.P3 spot mahazar shows that the spot of accident was Doddaballapura Dabaspet NH road running from east towards west and the accident had been taken place towards the northern side of the said road.
Further as per ExP3 on both side there was 5 feet mud road and there was a divider and as there was road repair works going on the southern end vehicles of both way were moving on the single road.
Under such facts when vehicles of both sides were moving on the single road, the driver of the Ape auto has to be careful and cautious.
ExP3 clearly shows that due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Ape auto accident had been taken place.
All these documents have not at all been challenged by the respondents.

Even the respondent has not examined the driver of the Ape auto who is the material witness to state as to the circumstances under which the accident has been taken place and tried to disprove the evidence of PW1.Though PW1 was cross examined, but nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW1.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Ex.P4 IMV report indicates that the occurrence of the said accident was not due to any of the mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.

13. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari vs Amir Chand & Ors  wherein it has been held that  "In a situation of this nature,
the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.

entities.text: AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari vs Amir Chand & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
14. Thus, the oral evidence of PW1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
15. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA439355.
16.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

entities.text: MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
17. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle Ape Auto bearing Reg.No.KA43 9355.

The petitioner to prove the injuries sustained by him in the accident has produced Ex.P5,
Ex.P7 to 24 which are Wound certificate, Discharge summaries, Lab reports, OPD card, medical bills, advance bills, medical prescriptions, adhaar card, x rays, medical bills, CD and photos.

Kantharaju.H vs Ramesh H.P on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189372859/
4
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

18. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 24 years.
The petitioner has produced the Aadhar card as per Ex.P.14 and the same discloses the date of birth of the petitioner as 19.02.1997 and the accident took place on 20.01.2022.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 24 years.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to the accident he was hale and healthy, doing agriculture and business and earning Rs.30,000/ p.m..
Due to accidental injuries, petitioner has lost the earnings.
In support of the same, petitioner has not produced any document to prove the avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of work, if the income is assessed at Rs.15,500/ p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
19. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:

As per the medical records, the petitioner has sustained fracture of left shaft of humerus, left patela fracture with bone exposure exteriously,
left inter condylor fracture of the femur.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex. P7 to 9discharge summaries discloses that petitioner has undergone treatment of ORIF with IMIL nailing for femur, ORIF with tension band wiring for the right patella and ORIF for the intercondylar fracture.
Petitioner was inpatient in the said hospital from 20.01.2022 to 28.01.2022 for 9 days.

Thereafter, due to infection and nonunion, petitioner got admitted to RMV hospital on 01.08.2022 to 482022 and underwent exchange nailing for the left femur and was inpatient on 13.07.2022 for one day.
Petitioner was inpatient totally for a period of 14 days.
20. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.

Therefore petitioner got examined one witness by name A.Chandrashekar, Medical Record Keeper at Rajmahal Vilas hospital, Sanjaynagar, Bengaluru, as PW.2 and he got marked authorisation letter, MLC extract, Admission records, Xrays as per Ex.P25 to 29.
21.
Further petitioner has examined Srinivas as PW.3 and he got marked police intimation, MLC register, Letter dt. 15.06.2023 and Xray at Ex.P33 to 36 documents.
22. Dr. Nagaraj B.N., Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre, as PW4 who has produced Ex P31 OPD slip and Ex.P32 Xray.

23. PW.4 in his examination in chief has stated that he examined the petitioner on 05.01.2018 for assessment of disability and finds that petitioner is unable to walk normally, unable to sit down,
squat and sit cross leg and has limping gait, painful rotations at the hip, restricted left knee movements, wasting of the left thigh muscles and the recent xray of the left femur and knee shows united fractures with implant insitu.

PW4 assessed disability of left lower limb at 51% and Kantharaju.H vs Ramesh H.P on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189372859/
5

permanent physical disability at 17%.
24.
Even in the cross examination PW2 stated that he has not treated the patient/petitioner.
The fractures are united.
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.4 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another.
25.

entities.text: Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though petitioner has stated that he was doing agriculture and business and earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.,and due to the injuries, he has lost his income.
Nevertheless petitioner has sustained fractures and certainly petitioner might face difficulty in carrying out his work.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, looking into the nature of work, age, gravity of the injury , the petitioner has to face some difficulty and functional disability and discomfort in order to do the work.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 15%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 15%.
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of above 24 age is '18'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/ a.m.

Hence a sum of Rs.5,02,200/
(Rs.15,500 x 12 x 18 x 15/100) is awarded under this head.

26. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P5, the petitioner has sustained fracture of left shaft of humerus, left patela fracture with bone exposure exteriously, left inter condylor fracture of the femur and undergone treatment of ORIF with IMIL nailing for femur, ORIF with tension band wiring for the right patella and ORIF for the intercondylar fracture and due to infection and non union, once again underwent exchange nailing for the left femur.
The doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner has sustained the injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and he has taken the treatment as inpatient for 14 days.
The petitioner has stated that due to accidental injuries he is facing difficulty to carryout his work.
Hence petitioner is suffering from with whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being aged 24 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.75,000/ under this head.

27. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAIDUP PERIOD:
Kantharaju.H vs Ramesh H.P on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189372859/
6

By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by her and duration of his stay in the hospital for 14 days as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 5 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.77,500/ (15,500 x 5) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.

28. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Doddabelavangala, Bengaluru Rural district and has taken the treatment at Government hospital, Doddaballapura and RMV hospital, Sanjaynagar, Bengaluru,
and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital.

Admittedly,
petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for 14 days and undergone treatment and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/ under this head.

29. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/ is awarded under this head.
30. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked medicals bills of Rs.1,89,398/, Rs.500/ and Rs.450/ as per Ex.P12, Ex.P16 and Ex.P17 respectively and medical prescriptions at Ex.P13.
The respondent has not disputed the said medical bills, except denial suggestion.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.1,90,348/(Rs.1,89,398/, Rs.500/ and Rs.450/) under the head of medical expenses.
31. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
PW4 doctor has stated that petitioner may need another surgery for removal of implant the estimate of surgery is around Rs.60,000/.
The petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 14 days and undergone operation.

Hence by considering the say of the doctor and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and future medical expenses required to the petitioner and also for other incidental charges i.e.,
for traveling expenses, food and other charges, this tribunal awarding Rs.50,000/
Kantharaju.H vs Ramesh H.P on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189372859/
7 under the head future medical expenses.
32.

The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of future income :
5,02,200/ due to disability 2 Pain & sufferings :
75,000/ 3 Loss of income during :
77,500/ laidup period 4

Attendant charges, extra :
25,000/ nutritious food & conveyance charges 5 Loss of future amenities :
25,000/ & happiness

6 Medical expenses :
 7

Future medical : 50,000/
 expenses

Total 7,54,700/
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,54,700/.
33.
INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
34. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

The counsel for the respondent argued that as on the date of accident, the offending vehicle was not having the valid fitness certificate and thereby owner of the vehicle respondent No.1 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy and hence respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
In support of his contention, counsel for the respondent No.2 examined the RTO as RW1 and got marked ExR1 and ExR2.
As per RW1 the offending vehicle Ape auto was having the FC from 2972018 till 2972020 and as on the date of the accident on 2012022 the said vehicle was not having the valid FC.
35. In this regard in respect to the fitness certificate is concerned, admittedly as per ExR2 the same has not been renewed from 2972020.

Even if there is no valid FC as on the date of the accident, it is not the defence available for the insurance company under section 149(2) of the Act and it is not the condition which is mentioned in the policy.
But it is only an offence under MV Act and insurance company cannot escape from the liability.

36. The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA439355 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable Kantharaju.H vs Ramesh H.P on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189372859/
8 to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
37. Issue No.3: In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,54,700/ with interest @ 6% p.a.
on Rs.7,04,700/ from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(Future medical expenses shall not carry interest).
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another.
25.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, looking into the nature of work, age, gravity of the injury , the petitioner has to face some difficulty and functional disability and discomfort in order to do the work.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 15%, cannot be ruled out.
The petitioner has sustained the injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and he has taken the treatment as inpatient for 14 days.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
34. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
The counsel for the respondent argued that as on the date of accident, the offending vehicle was not having the valid fitness certificate and thereby owner of the vehicle respondent No.1 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy and hence respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
Even if there is no valid FC as on the date of the accident, it is not the defence available for the insurance company under section 149(2) of the Act and it is not the condition which is mentioned in the policy.
But it is only an offence under MV Act and insurance company cannot escape from the liability.

36. The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA439355 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable Kantharaju.H vs Ramesh H.P on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189372859/
8 to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
37. Issue No.3: In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,54,700/ with interest @ 6% p.a.
on Rs.7,04,700/ from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(Future medical expenses shall not carry interest).
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
